title: Punjab reorganised, 1966
hookLine: Punjab is reorganised into a smaller Punjabi-speaking state

cards: A map is redrawn, and overnight a village's address changes without a single house moving. That is what happened across Punjab in the year in today's title. One state was cut into parts.
Lines were drawn through districts, and families woke up in a new state, or in the same state with a new shape.
For the Sikhs who had marched and gone to jail for it, the answer had finally come: a Punjab where Punjabi was the language of the state. A smaller Punjab, and a home for a language.

teach.b: First, the new lines. The Punjabi-speaking areas became the new, smaller Punjab. Hindi-speaking areas became a new state, Haryana.
Some hill districts were joined to Himachal Pradesh. Second, what it gave.

teach.h: PUNJABI IN GURMUKHI, THE STATE'S LANGUAGE.
teach.b: Punjabi, written in Gurmukhi, became the language of the state: of its schools, its offices, its signboards.

Gurmukhi is the script the Guru Granth Sahib is written in, and tradition credits Guru Angad, the second Guru, with shaping it for the Sikhs. So the letters a child learned at school were the letters of the Guru's word.

teach.h: CHANDIGARH AND THE RIVERS LEFT OPEN.
teach.b: Third, what it left open. The new city of Chandigarh was not simply handed to Punjab; it became a shared capital for Punjab and Haryana.
Questions about river waters and borders stayed unsettled, and they come back in the days ahead.

teach.h: FROM PARTITION TO A LANGUAGE HOME.
teach.b: Some Sikhs felt they had won the language and lost some of what they had asked for alongside it. Fourth, a look back. This week began on the trains of Partition.

Then came Nankana Sahib, left behind across a new border; families starting again by kirat; a poet mourning Punjab's daughters; Bhagat Puran Singh carrying a boy on his back; and the long campaign of asking.
A week that started with a border cutting Punjab apart ends with a border drawn on purpose, around a language.

how: Sikhs and other Punjabis remember the reorganization of Punjab as the end of the Punjabi Suba campaign; Punjabi in Gurmukhi is taught in Punjab's schools and used in its government.

practice: Whatever language you first heard as a child, bring it back now, and silently say one word from it: the word for mother, or home, or water, or bread.

Breathe in with that word, breathe out and notice who said it to you first; if English is your first language, find the oldest word you remember from a grandparent's mouth. If you pray, Waheguru is a word to rest on too.

wordCard.voice: Punjab reorganised. The old state redrawn into a smaller Punjab where Punjabi, in Gurmukhi, became the language of the state, with Haryana and Himachal taking the rest. Today's word.

orig.note: mother tongue; the language you first heard at home.

carryVoice: Your line: the language home. The letters of school, the letters of the Guru's word. A good week's end.
